text.p: These are the leading stories in Botswana's independent midweek newspapers, The Sun and The Gazette, on Wednesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The Office of the President and the Department of Foreign Affairs are formulating a response to a request from South Africa to have a sitting of the Truth and Reconciliation Commission in Botswana. There have been recent allegations that some Batswana spied for the former South African government.

- An unmarried mother has won the right to sue in the High Court for maintenance in excess of the previously accepted 40 pula per month for each of her two minor children, both fathered by the same man.

- The Gaborone Private Hospital is negotiating out of court settlements with two nurses forced to undergo HIV testing, and who tested positive and were subsequently firted. HIV testing in Botswana is, by law, voluntary in all cases.

- The South African Department of Foreign Affairs is materminding a scheme for countries of the 12-member Southern African Development Community (SADC) to share overseas missions. South African High Commissioner in Botswama Oupa Mokou confirmed the issue "had been discussed" at a SADC officials meeting in Gaborone, but Botswana Foreign Affairs officials say they were not advised of the meeting.
